title: Protocol for multiplex fluorescent immunohistochemistry in free-floating rodent brain tissues
protocol: Rinse tissue in 0.1 M PBS on a shaker for 5 minutes.
Repeat rinsing the tissue in fresh 0.1 M PBS five times using new well plates each time.
Transfer tissue between wells using a paint brush.
Make a 1× PBS solution with 10% normal donkey serum and 0.3% Triton X-100.
Pipette 500 μL of blocking buffer into each of 12 wells in a new well plate.
Transfer tissue from the final PBS rinse into the well plate containing blocking buffer.
Place the well plate in a humid chamber.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 h.
Mix donkey serum in 0.1 M PBS with a stir bar spinning on a stir plate.
Add Triton X-100 via pipette and allow to completely dissolve for at least 2 minutes.
Make a 1× PBS solution with 5% normal donkey serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 in a glass beaker.
Store the diluent at 4°C for one week.
Mix primary antibodies into diluent.
Pipette 500 μL of the primary antibody solution into each of 12 wells in a new well plate.
Transfer tissue directly from the blocking buffer into the well plate containing the primary antibody solution.
Place the well plate in a humid chamber and incubate at 4°C for 24 h.
Rinse tissue in fresh 0.1 M PBS on a shaker.
Rinse tissue for 30 min in fresh 0.1 M PBS on a shaker.
Repeat tissue rinsing, step 16 a.
Mix biotin into diluent to prepare the biotin solution.
Pipette 500 μL of primary antibody solution into each of 12 wells in a new well plate.
Transfer rinsed tissues into a new well plate containing the biotin solution.
Incubate the well plate in a humid chamber at room temperature for 1 hour.
Rinse tissue in fresh 0.1 M PBS on a shaker.
Rinse tissue for 15 minutes in fresh 0.1 M PBS on a shaker.
Repeat tissue rinsing step as needed.
Incubate tissues with secondary antibody solution for 2 hours.
Mix secondary antibodies into diluent at concentrations of 1:150 for donkey anti-mouse 680, 1:300 for donkey anti-rabbit 594, and 1:300 for streptavidin 488.
Pipette 500 μL of primary antibody solution into each of 12 wells in a new well plate.
Transfer tissue from the rinse into the well plate containing the secondary antibody solution.
Place the well plate in a humid chamber in the dark at room temperature for 2 hours.
Rinse tissue in fresh 0.1 M PBS on a shaker.
Cover well plate with a box lid to protect from light.
Rinse tissue for 10 min in fresh 0.1 M PBS on a shaker.
Cover well plate with a box lid to protect from light.
Repeat tissue rinsing, step 28a.
Mount tissues on microscope slides by distributing them across 0.1 M PBS-filled well plates.
Gently lift tissues using a paint brush to ensure they adhere properly to the slide.
Hold the paint brush parallel to the slide and press it against the slide while rolling it clockwise to transfer the tissue.
Use a 0.1 M PBS-saturated paint brush to gently move the tissue so that it lies completely flat on the slide.
Cover the slides with coverslips and allow them to dry for 24 hours before sealing and imaging.
Ensure all individual tissue sections reach the crystalline stage once prior to moving to the next step.
Rewet tissue by gently dabbing 0.1 M PBS onto the tissue section with a paint brush.
Pipette approximately 3 drops of mounting medium (e.g., Prolong Gold with DAPI) evenly across the slide.
Gently place the left side of a coverslip onto the left side of the slide.
Use forceps to slowly lower the right side of the coverslip onto the slide.
If tissue sections substantially slide and overlap, immediately place the entire slide into a dish of 0.1 M PBS.
With the slide submerged in PBS, gently slide off the coverslip; all tissue will detach and float in the dish.
Start the mounting process anew if necessary.
Place coverslipped slides on a paper towel under a box lid to dry for 24 hours.
Seal coverslipped slides after drying.
Apply clear nail polish around the edges of the coverslip to seal the gap between the coverslip and the slide.
Store slides at room temperature in light-blocking slide boxes for imaging.
Hold a small dish of 0.1 M PBS with tissue sections floating in it if using an alternative mounting method.
Submerge the slide mostly parallel to the water and slightly below the surface of the PBS solution.
Scoot the tissue onto the slide with a paint brush.
Mount tissue using desktop stereo microscopes, ensuring no tissue is folded over or overlapping.
